item.title: Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling
item.description:
Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling

In an interview on the Colin and Samir podcast, Instagram head Adam Mosseri addressed growing anxiety surrounding artificial intelligence, discussing creator concerns, platform ranking, and Instagram’s policies on AI-generated content.

🔍 Overview

Mosseri acknowledged that negativity surrounding AI is “going to get worse” and will continue to intensify over the next couple of years, particularly across creative industries. He noted that while some frustration and anger is founded and some unfounded, the underlying sentiment across various fields comes down to “a fear of being left behind in some way.”

⚙️ Content Ranking and Policies

Mosseri detailed how Instagram approaches AI-generated material and profiles on the platform:

  • AI Ranking Quality: Instagram does not rank AI creators differently, but Mosseri indicated the platform likely does not rank AI content as well as non-AI content due to quality variations. He noted there is both “great AI content” and “AI slop,” though he believes the term “slop” is used “too liberally.”
  • No Banning Strategy: Instagram is actively working on solutions for misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes, but Mosseri stated, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”
  • Account Labeling: Following an initial label launch earlier this year and a crackdown on AI-generated profiles in August, Instagram is starting to require AI accounts to label themselves so users can distinguish between real and un-real content.

💡 Key Concerns Identified

During the interview, Mosseri outlined specific fears expressed by creators and professionals:

  • Content Rights: Concerns over creators owning their content and models being trained on that content.
  • Safety and Displacement: Fears regarding platform safety and job displacement affecting content creators, engineers, and mathematicians.

#Instagram #Meta #GenerativeAI #SocialMedia #AIContent

Source: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’

item.title: Meta Delays New Business Terms Again Amid Publisher Concerns Over AI Training
item.description:
Meta Delays New Business Terms Again Amid Publisher Concerns Over AI Training

Meta has announced it may delay the implementation of its new business terms past the November 20th deadline as the company faces backlash from publishers regarding AI training practices. The company has stated it does not plan to implement these policy changes without a full consultation with industry groups and leaders, a process that may delay enforcement indefinitely.

🔍 Overview

  • Original Effective Date: October 30th.
  • First Delay: Postponed to November 20th.
  • Current Status: Likely to be delayed beyond November 20th as consultations continue.
  • Active Terms: Meta’s existing business terms will remain in place until the updated version is implemented.

⚙️ Key details

The controversy surrounds updated business terms that initially appeared to grant Meta permission to train its AI models on news sites that utilize Facebook and Instagram. While Meta later removed specific language regarding “training” products on content scraped from these sites, legal experts from Nieman Lab have noted that the updated policy still does not explicitly rule out the possibility.

Meta communications head Andy Stone addressed the situation on X, stating, “We’ve heard publishers’ feedback on our proposed ads and business terms update. We’re committed to getting this right, and as we expect this consultation could extend beyond November 20, in which case we’d delay implementation of the updated terms.”

💡 Why it matters

The proposed changes have drawn significant opposition from industry organizations and government officials who are concerned about the exploitation of content for AI development.

Stakeholder Position or Action
Andy Stone (Meta) Committed to a full consultation with industry leaders before policy changes.
Legal Experts (Nieman Lab) Noted that policy revisions are currently insufficient to rule out AI training.
News/Media Alliance Provided pushback against the proposed business terms.
Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) Stated the terms indicate Meta is attempting to exploit American creators and businesses.
Sen. Adam Schiff (D-CA) Urged Meta to reverse the proposed policy changes.

#Meta #AITraining #DigitalPublishing #TechPolicy

Source: Meta says it’ll probably delay its controversial new business terms again

item.title: Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic
item.description:
Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode Reduce Publisher Traffic

Publishers spent years figuring out how to get clicks on Google, building a reciprocal relationship where they supplied content and Google supplied exposure. In 2024 and 2025 Google introduced AI‑driven search features that have reshaped that relationship and sharply lowered traffic to many news sites.

🔍 Overview

  • AI Overviews (2024) – An AI‑generated summary appears at the very top of Google Search, followed by links to sources the AI deems most useful. [Evidence]
  • AI Mode (May 2025) – Replaces standard search with a chatbot‑like interface that provides detailed summaries from web results. [Evidence]
  • The features change how results are ranked and displayed, making it harder for publishers to rely on Google traffic alone. [Evidence]

🗓️ Timeline

Year Feature Key Change
2024 AI Overviews AI‑generated summary placed at top of results with source links below.
2025 AI Mode Standard search replaced by a chatbot‑style interface that returns detailed summaries.

📉 Impact on Publishers

  • News outlets that spent time and money optimizing pages for clicks saw traffic tank after the AI features launched. [Evidence]
  • The Wall Street Journal (June 2025) reported declines for Business Insider, The Washington Post, HuffPost, and the WSJ itself since 2022. [Evidence]
  • Similarweb data showed The New York Times’ search traffic fell from 44 % to 35.5 % over three years. [Evidence]
  • DCN reported 19 members lost 1–25 % of Google traffic between May and June 2025. [Evidence]
  • DMG Media (Daily Mail, Metro) told the UK CMA click‑through rates dropped up to 89 % between June and July 2025, citing AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • Pew Research found users are less likely to click on external links when an AI Overview is shown. [Evidence]
  • The News/Media Alliance warned AI Overviews would be “catastrophic” for web traffic. [Evidence]

🛠️ Google’s Response

  • Offered a toggle that lets sites opt out of appearing in AI Overviews and AI Mode without losing standard search visibility (rolled out after a UK order). [Evidence]
  • Made source links more prominent: hovering over a link shows a pop‑up with article titles and images. [Evidence]
  • Added another AI change that puts in‑line links higher up in responses more frequently. [Evidence]
  • Google’s leadership statements: Liz Reid said click volume remained “relatively stable,” while Nick Fox said “from our point of view, the web is thriving.” [Evidence]

⚖️ Legal and Regulatory Context

  • US District Judge Amit Mehta dismissed an antitrust suit from Chegg and Penske Media and rejected a class‑action claim from Arkansas newspapers over AI Overviews. [Evidence]
  • The UK Competition and Markets Authority received complaints from DMG Media about click‑through declines linked to AI Overviews. [Evidence]

The rollout of AI Overviews and AI Mode marks a significant shift in Google Search, turning a long‑standing traffic source into a more opaque AI‑mediated layer and prompting measurable traffic losses across the digital publishing ecosystem.

#GoogleAI #DigitalPublishing #SearchTraffic #AIOverviews

Source: Google’s AI search changes upended online publishing

item.title: YouTube adds AI disclosure label to music tracks
item.description:
YouTube adds AI disclosure label to music tracks

YouTube is rolling out a “Made with AI” label for music tracks that were altered or fully generated using generative AI, beginning in the YouTube Music app and later expanding to the main YouTube app.

🔍 Overview

  • The label appears on tracks that were “altered or fully generated” with AI.
  • It mirrors YouTube’s existing process for applying AI labels to videos.
  • The goal is to give listeners clear information about AI‑generated music.

⚙️ How it works

  • Music partners must disclose generative AI use when uploading songs.
  • If no disclosure is provided, YouTube may use “other signals” to decide if a song is AI‑generated.
  • YouTube combines partner disclosures with its own detection tools to identify AI‑generated tracks.
  • When AI played a significant role, a label is shown directly on the player page.
  • Tapping the label opens a simple menu that shares more information.

🚀 Availability

  • The label is rolling out starting today in the YouTube Music app.
  • It will expand to the main YouTube app later.

📊 Industry context

Platform AI Label Action
Spotify Launched a voluntary AI label earlier this year and said it wouldn’t recommend songs from “AI personas.”
Apple Music Reportedly getting an AI tag.
Deezer Added a switch for filtering out AI tracks.
Bandcamp Banned AI music outright earlier this year.

💡 Why it matters

  • YouTube wants it to be as easy as possible for listeners to have the right information and clarity when it comes to the music they listen to.
  • The label helps differentiate AI‑generated content from human‑created music, supporting informed choice.

#YouTube #AI #Music #Labeling

Source: YouTube sticks new labels on AI-generated songs

item.title: YouTube Announces AI Agent and New Creator Optimization Tools
item.description:
YouTube Announces AI Agent and New Creator Optimization Tools

At the annual Made on YouTube event, the company announced updates to the suite of AI-powered creator tools it first unveiled in 2025.

⚙️ Key details

YouTube is introducing an AI “agent” designed to optimize a creator’s channel in the background. Its capabilities include:

  • Catalog Monitoring: The tool monitors back catalogs for content that is trending, relevant to the news, or has taken on a new life, offering suggestions for title and thumbnail tweaks.
  • Content Generation: The agent can generate entire titles and thumbnails based on an uploaded video’s content.
  • Creator Feedback: Creators can request feedback from the tool regarding their own thumbnails.
  • Brand Pitching: According to Amjad Hanif, vice president of creator products at YouTube, the tool can create brand pitches by pulling demographic and audience data from a creator’s channel.

🧩 How it works

YouTube is introducing several A/B testing and optimization features to boost watch time:

Feature Function
Dynamic Thumbnails Assigns one of up to three uploaded images to different audience segments.
Video Testing Tests three versions of a video (e.g., different hooks or structures) with small audience segments.

Regarding video testing, Hanif says the system ensures the three versions are not “dramatically different.” Creators can manually select a “winner” version or allow YouTube to do so automatically after seven days.

#YouTube #AIagents #ContentCreation #VideoOptimization

Source: YouTube is building AI creator tools that do almost everything for them

item.title: Internal Documents Reveal Microsoft and OpenAI Concerns Over AI Content Strategy
item.description:
Internal Documents Reveal Microsoft and OpenAI Concerns Over AI Content Strategy

Internal documents and employee statements from Microsoft and OpenAI indicate that the companies’ AI content strategy may be damaging the web and the economic foundations of the data sources used to train their models.

💡 Why it matters

Internal Microsoft documentation describes a “doom loop” where the company’s AI content strategy threatens the “content supply chain” by creating an end-product that threatens its essential suppliers. Key concerns include:

  • Supply Chain Impact: Microsoft admitted that “LLMs are a product that destroys its own supply chain” because they can act as a substitute for the training data they rely on.
  • Web Traffic Decline: OpenAI experts attributed a drop in referral traffic for sites like the Times directly to AI summaries; they speculated search referrals may be down as much as 60 percent.
  • User Behavior: Satya Nadella admitted chatbots have basically replaced search and removed the need to go straight to the source. OpenAI’s Nick Turley stated that once a user gets an answer from a chatbot, there is “no good reason to click” on a source link.

⚙️ Key details

Documents and employees have highlighted several issues regarding data acquisition and model output:

  • Data Scraping: Hecht characterized the harvesting of data for ChatGPT and Copilot as the “largest theft of labor in human history” and claimed Microsoft’s defense makes a “complete mockery of the idea of ‘fair use.’”
  • Content Regurgitation: Employees admitted GPT-4 “memorized a ton of data and therefore will be insanely good at regurgitation.” Examples show ChatGPT outputting long strings of copy from the Times, Mercury News, The Denver Post, LifeHacker, and Eurogamer.
  • Paywalls: An OpenAI representative admitted to being “unaware” of any effort to remove paywalled content from training data.
  • Labor Impact: OpenAI Policy Director Jack Clark stated the company was “creating systems that substitute for the labor of the people that define the ‘culture’ of society.”

🔍 Perspectives

Person/Entity Viewpoint
Hecht Characterized scraping as the “largest theft of labor in human history.”
Alex Haurek (Microsoft) Stated Hecht’s comments reflect an individual perspective and not the company’s views.
Jordan Usdan (Microsoft) Characterized Hecht’s role as adversarial.
Greg Brockman (OpenAI) Described as more interested in the “gazillions” of dollars potentially made through commercial AI.

#Microsoft #OpenAI #LLM #AIEthics #DataScraping

Source: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web

item.title: Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall
item.description:
Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall

AI firm Fountain 0 has released a new film titled Odysseus: The Fall, which is described as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Production: Written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who created all the music and lent his likeness to the title character.
  • Motivation: Koosha stated he adapted the story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.”
  • Studio History: The studio’s only previous work was an AI film called Dreams of Violets that was featured in Tribeca earlier this year.

🚀 Availability

  • Price: Available to rent for $9.99.
  • Platform: Viewable via a web browser.

🔍 Observations

Because current AI models are only capable of generating scenes lasting a few seconds, the film is described as a disjointed collection of moments stitched together. Reported technical and narrative issues include:

  • Visual Inconsistencies: The height of the cyclops changes between shots, oars bend and twist, a sword transforms into a dagger, and waves move in the opposite direction of the wind.
  • Animation Errors: Mouths do not match spoken words (sometimes moving without sound), and one boat in a fleet is seen moving sideways.
  • Audio Issues: AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and the names of Zeus and Odysseus are pronounced incorrectly.
  • Character and Plot: Characters exhibit baffling acting with unexplained pauses and bursts of laughter. The plot structure is disjointed, with Penelope’s suitors not introduced until the movie is nearly over.
  • Visual Style: Hyperreal human characters are contrasted with monsters that look like “shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s.”
  • Anomalies: One scene features an alien carcass roasting over a spit.

#Fountain0 #GenerativeAI #AIFilm #OdysseusTheFall

Source: The 2.5-hour AI-generated Odyssey movie is 2.5 hours too long
